class="prose prose--block prose--blog col-span-full!"><p>Today we identified a security incident involving a specific extension in the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace: <strong>Anthropic.claude-code version 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for Windows and MacOS</strong>. These malicious versions of the extension were not developed by Anthropic. This does not impact other extensions downloaded from the cursor.com/marketplace, Grok Bot, Grok or our other SpaceXSI products.</p>
<h2 id="what-happened" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#what-happened" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>What happened</h2>
<p>Between about 2:27am PT and 1:35pm PT today, a maliciously modified version of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension was made available in the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace. The extension runs malicious code that attempts to install a persistent SSH backdoor. Specifically, it:</p>
<ul>
<li>Collects and reports host and user information: hostname, username, OS, architecture, home directory path, environment variable names, working directories, configured Git email, and public IP.</li>
<li>Attempts to add an attacker-controlled SSH key to <code>authorized_keys</code>, enable the local SSH service, and open a reverse SSH tunnel. Outside of highly unusual circumstances where Cursor was started with administrator privileges, due to errors in the malicious code, this step would fail.</li>
<li>Attempts to make the reverse SSH tunnel persistent via a LaunchAgent (macOS), or a scheduled task that attempts to run as SYSTEM with a Startup-script fallback (Windows). Background scripts retry the tunnel roughly every 60 seconds.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Note: The attacker server no longer functions.</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>We worked with the cloud provider that was hosting it to take it offline, so the reverse shell and host detail POST are not functional.</li>
<li>These findings concern the identified package. We have no evidence that other versions of the extension or the official distribution are affected.</li>
<li>Additionally, turning on the local SSH service requires admin rights, which the malicious extension does not have on most macOS and Windows hosts. On those hosts the step fails and the attacker could not have logged in through the tunnel. The extension added the attacker’s SSH key, installed persistence, and sent host details to the attacker. Follow the remediation steps below regardless.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="what-we-did" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#what-we-did" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>What we did</h2>
<ul>
<li>Removed the malicious version from the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace immediately upon detection and blocked further distribution. We followed with a full shut down of the marketplace out of an abundance of caution.</li>
<li>We audited access and confirmed no other extensions were tampered with.</li>
<li>We rotated our keys, rebuilt the marketplace, and brought it back online.</li>
<li>We worked with the hosting provider to take the malicious server offline, disrupting the attack by blocking the connection to that server.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="what-you-should-do" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#what-you-should-do" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>What you should do</h2>
<p>If you installed or updated to Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 from the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace on macOS or Windows between 2:27am PT and 1:35pm PT on October 29, 2026:</p>
<ol>
<li>Run the attached script to validate if you are impacted (see below).</li>
<li>Search across endpoint, network, and extension-installation telemetry for the indicators below.</li>
<li>Isolate hosts showing evidence of payload execution or backdoor installation.</li>
<li>Remove the unauthorized SSH key, persistence mechanisms, and running tunnel processes, and assess whether the host should be rebuilt. Uninstalling the extension may not be sufficient — the payload drops standalone persistence scripts that keep running.</li>
<li>Rotate credentials and sessions accessible from affected hosts, from a trusted system. The limited env-var collection does not rule out later credential access over the backdoor.</li>
</ol>
<h2 id="check-whether-you-are-impacted" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#check-whether-you-are-impacted" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Check whether you are impacted</h2>
<p>The malicious extension appends the attacker&#x27;s public key, labeled <code>svc-telemetry</code>, to your SSH authorized keys. To check for it:</p>
<p>On macOS, run:</p>
<div class="prose-code-block"><pre class="shiki shiki-themes github-light github-dark" style="background-color:#fff;--shiki-dark-bg:#24292e;color:#24292e;--shiki-dark:#e1e4e8" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1;--shiki-dark:#B392F0">grep</span><span style="color:#005CC5;--shiki-dark:#79B8FF"> -qs</span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF"> svc-telemetry</span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF"> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> &amp;&amp; </span><span style="color:#005CC5;--shiki-dark:#79B8FF">echo</span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF"> &quot;svc-telemetry key found&quot;</span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583"> ||</span><span style="color:#005CC5;--shiki-dark:#79B8FF"> echo</span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF"> &quot;No key found; machine not impacted&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>On Windows, run in PowerShell:</p>
<div class="prose-code-block"><pre class="shiki shiki-themes github-light github-dark" style="background-color:#fff;--shiki-dark-bg:#24292e;color:#24292e;--shiki-dark:#e1e4e8" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8">$files </span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">=</span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF"> &quot;</span><span style="color:#005CC5;--shiki-dark:#79B8FF">$HOME</span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF">\.ssh\authorized_keys&quot;</span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">,</span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF"> &quot;C:\ProgramData\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys&quot;</span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583"> |</span><span style="color:#005CC5;--shiki-dark:#79B8FF"> Where-Object</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> { </span><span style="color:#005CC5;--shiki-dark:#79B8FF">Test-Path</span><span style="color:#005CC5;--shiki-dark:#79B8FF"> $_</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> }</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">if</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> ($files </span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">-and</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> (</span><span style="color:#005CC5;--shiki-dark:#79B8FF">Select-String</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> svc</span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">-</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8">telemetry $files)) { </span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF">&quot;svc-telemetry key found&quot;</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> } </span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">else</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> { </span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF">&quot;No key found; machine not impacted&quot;</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> }</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>If the key is found, your machine is impacted. Follow steps 3 to 5 above, and run the remediation script for your platform below.</p>
<h2 id="remediate-affected-machines" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#remediate-affected-machines" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Remediate affected machines</h2>
<p>These scripts remove the malicious extension, the persistence mechanisms, the running tunnel processes, and the attacker&#x27;s SSH key. They exit with a non-zero status if anything remains.</p>
<p>On macOS, download <a href="/static/security/claude-code-extension/remediate-macos.sh" download="">remediate-macos.sh</a> and run it as the affected user, not as root, from the folder you saved it to:</p>
<div class="prose-code-block"><pre class="shiki shiki-themes github-light github-dark" style="background-color:#fff;--shiki-dark-bg:#24292e;color:#24292e;--shiki-dark:#e1e4e8" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1;--shiki-dark:#B392F0">bash</span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF"> remediate-macos.sh</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>On Windows, download <a href="/static/security/claude-code-extension/remediate-windows.ps1" download="">remediate-windows.ps1</a> and run it from PowerShell opened with <strong>Run as Administrator</strong>, in the folder you saved it to:</p>
<div class="prose-code-block"><pre class="shiki shiki-themes github-light github-dark" style="background-color:#fff;--shiki-dark-bg:#24292e;color:#24292e;--shiki-dark:#e1e4e8" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8">powershell </span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">-</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8">ExecutionPolicy Bypass </span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">-</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8">File .\remediate</span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">-</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8">windows.ps1</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h2 id="indicators-of-compromise" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#indicators-of-compromise" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Indicators of compromise</h2>

<li>Modified VSIX SHA-256 (win32-x64): 6786ec90cbd45949695bd7805c9fbb26cfc91bc5fc897de0183d9bcb9cb21731 (MD5 7838a3be2ca0ff08c1bdb160ef516d39)</li>

<h3 id="payload" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#payload" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Payload</h3>
<ul>
<li>Modified code: extension.js in package versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for both Darwin and Windows in the extension folder contains 134[.]209[.]82[.]225 and svc-telemetry</li>
<li>SHA-256: ecb58cb29078d9646ad1dcdbe51526f2d9cfea06be5fb2ab183e8ecc3ab6bf15</li>
<li>MD5: f49bcd657ef1e626e85ce858958c1769</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="network" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#network" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Network</h3>
<ul>
<li>Attacker endpoint: 134[.]209[.]82[.]225</li>
<li>Reverse SSH: tunnel@134[.]209[.]82[.]225, TCP 22</li>
<li>External beacon: hxxp://134[.]209[.]82[.]225:8099/beacon (HTTP POST)</li>
<li>Local beacon attempt: 127[.]0[.]0[.]1:8099/beacon (HTTP POST, loopback)</li>
<li>Public IP lookups to ifconfig[.]me / api[.]ipify[.]org — legitimate services; access alone is not an indicator</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="ssh" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#ssh" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>SSH</h3>
<ul>
<li>Unauthorized public key: <code>ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIDdvylCEJ/k2TpezcTfedrkHyFSK9IZ3vmP6vhY4Ss0P svc-telemetry</code></li>
<li>Unauthorized key fingerprint: <code>SHA256:0Z6R+DF64Do2nwQic8a7kkfDLNNk4IiK+2U2Rci4htk</code></li>
<li>Reverse-tunnel key fingerprint: <code>SHA256:KOAU57+ZG6u3MG4WwzPzPX2O5YEe9qdOC1Bl+6MVyDQ</code></li>
<li>Key comment: <code>svc-telemetry</code></li>
</ul>
<h3 id="files-and-persistence" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#files-and-persistence" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Files and persistence</h3>
<ul>
<li>Linux / macOS: unauthorized key in <code>~/.ssh/authorized_keys</code>; <code>~/.config/.smt</code>, <code>~/.config/.smtk</code></li>
<li>Linux: <code>/tmp/.stk_&lt;10 hex&gt;</code>; cron <code>@reboot /bin/sh &quot;&lt;HOME&gt;/.config/.smt&quot;</code></li>
<li>macOS: <code>$TMPDIR/.stk_&lt;10 hex&gt;</code>; <code>~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.apple.sysmond.plist</code> (label <code>com.apple.sysmond</code>)</li>
<li>Windows: <code>%USERPROFILE%\.ssh\authorized_keys</code>, <code>%USERPROFILE%\.config\smt.cmd</code>, <code>%USERPROFILE%\.config\smtk</code>, <code>%TEMP%\.stk_&lt;10 hex&gt;</code>; scheduled task <code>SysMon</code> (attempts to run as SYSTEM); fallback <code>%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\sysmon.cmd</code></li>
</ul>
<h3 id="process-command-line" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#process-command-line" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Process / command-line</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>ssh -N -R &#x27;*:0:localhost:22&#x27;</code>, <code>autossh -M 0</code></li>
<li>SSH options: <code>StrictHostKeyChecking=no</code>, <code>UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null</code>, <code>ServerAliveInterval=30</code>, <code>ServerAliveCountMax=3</code>, <code>ExitOnForwardFailure=yes</code>, <code>IdentitiesOnly=yes</code></li>
<li><code>schtasks /create /tn SysMon</code></li>
<li><code>systemsetup -setremotelogin on</code></li>
<li><code>Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Server~~~~0.0.1.0</code></li>
</ul>
<p>If you have further questions, reach out to <a href="mailto:security@cursor.com" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">security@cursor.com</a>.</p>

class="prose prose--block prose--blog col-span-full!"><p>Today we identified a security incident involving a specific extension in the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace: <strong>Anthropic.claude-code version 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for Windows and MacOS</strong>. These malicious versions of the extension were not developed by Anthropic. This does not impact other extensions downloaded from the cursor.com/marketplace, Grok Bot, Grok or our other SpaceXSI products.</p>
<h2 id="what-happened" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#what-happened" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>What happened</h2>
<p>Between about 2:27am PT and 1:35pm PT today, a maliciously modified version of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension was made available in the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace. The extension runs malicious code that attempts to install a persistent SSH backdoor. Specifically, it:</p>
<ul>
<li>Collects and reports host and user information: hostname, username, OS, architecture, home directory path, environment variable names, working directories, configured Git email, and public IP.</li>
<li>Attempts to add an attacker-controlled SSH key to <code>authorized_keys</code>, enable the local SSH service, and open a reverse SSH tunnel. Outside of highly unusual circumstances where Cursor was started with administrator privileges, due to errors in the malicious code, this step would fail.</li>
<li>Attempts to make the reverse SSH tunnel persistent via a LaunchAgent (macOS), or a scheduled task that attempts to run as SYSTEM with a Startup-script fallback (Windows). Background scripts retry the tunnel roughly every 60 seconds.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Note: The attacker server no longer functions.</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>We worked with the cloud provider that was hosting it to take it offline, so the reverse shell and host detail POST are not functional.</li>
<li>These findings concern the identified package. We have no evidence that other versions of the extension or the official distribution are affected.</li>
<li>Additionally, turning on the local SSH service requires admin rights, which the malicious extension does not have on most macOS and Windows hosts. On those hosts the step fails and the attacker could not have logged in through the tunnel. The extension added the attacker’s SSH key, installed persistence, and sent host details to the attacker. Follow the remediation steps below regardless.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="what-we-did" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#what-we-did" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>What we did</h2>
<ul>
<li>Removed the malicious version from the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace immediately upon detection and blocked further distribution. We followed with a full shut down of the marketplace out of an abundance of caution.</li>
<li>We audited access and confirmed no other extensions were tampered with.</li>
<li>We rotated our keys, rebuilt the marketplace, and brought it back online.</li>
<li>We worked with the hosting provider to take the malicious server offline, disrupting the attack by blocking the connection to that server.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="what-you-should-do" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#what-you-should-do" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>What you should do</h2>
<p>If you installed or updated to Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 from the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace on macOS or Windows between 2:27am PT and 1:35pm PT on October 29, 2026:</p>
<ol>
<li>Run the attached script to validate if you are impacted (see below).</li>
<li>Search across endpoint, network, and extension-installation telemetry for the indicators below.</li>
<li>Isolate hosts showing evidence of payload execution or backdoor installation.</li>
<li>Remove the unauthorized SSH key, persistence mechanisms, and running tunnel processes, and assess whether the host should be rebuilt. Uninstalling the extension may not be sufficient — the payload drops standalone persistence scripts that keep running.</li>
<li>Rotate credentials and sessions accessible from affected hosts, from a trusted system. The limited env-var collection does not rule out later credential access over the backdoor.</li>
</ol>
<h2 id="check-whether-you-are-impacted" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#check-whether-you-are-impacted" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Check whether you are impacted</h2>
<p>The malicious extension appends the attacker&#x27;s public key, labeled <code>svc-telemetry</code>, to your SSH authorized keys. To check for it:</p>
<p>On macOS, run:</p>
<div class="prose-code-block"><pre class="shiki shiki-themes github-light github-dark" style="background-color:#fff;--shiki-dark-bg:#24292e;color:#24292e;--shiki-dark:#e1e4e8" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1;--shiki-dark:#B392F0">grep</span><span style="color:#005CC5;--shiki-dark:#79B8FF"> -qs</span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF"> svc-telemetry</span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF"> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> &amp;&amp; </span><span style="color:#005CC5;--shiki-dark:#79B8FF">echo</span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF"> &quot;svc-telemetry key found&quot;</span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583"> ||</span><span style="color:#005CC5;--shiki-dark:#79B8FF"> echo</span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF"> &quot;No key found; machine not impacted&quot;</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>On Windows, run in PowerShell:</p>
<div class="prose-code-block"><pre class="shiki shiki-themes github-light github-dark" style="background-color:#fff;--shiki-dark-bg:#24292e;color:#24292e;--shiki-dark:#e1e4e8" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8">$files </span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">=</span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF"> &quot;</span><span style="color:#005CC5;--shiki-dark:#79B8FF">$HOME</span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF">\.ssh\authorized_keys&quot;</span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">,</span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF"> &quot;C:\ProgramData\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys&quot;</span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583"> |</span><span style="color:#005CC5;--shiki-dark:#79B8FF"> Where-Object</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> { </span><span style="color:#005CC5;--shiki-dark:#79B8FF">Test-Path</span><span style="color:#005CC5;--shiki-dark:#79B8FF"> $_</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> }</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">if</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> ($files </span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">-and</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> (</span><span style="color:#005CC5;--shiki-dark:#79B8FF">Select-String</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> svc</span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">-</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8">telemetry $files)) { </span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF">&quot;svc-telemetry key found&quot;</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> } </span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">else</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> { </span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF">&quot;No key found; machine not impacted&quot;</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8"> }</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>If the key is found, your machine is impacted. Follow steps 3 to 5 above, and run the remediation script for your platform below.</p>
<h2 id="remediate-affected-machines" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#remediate-affected-machines" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Remediate affected machines</h2>
<p>These scripts remove the malicious extension, the persistence mechanisms, the running tunnel processes, and the attacker&#x27;s SSH key. They exit with a non-zero status if anything remains.</p>
<p>On macOS, download <a href="/static/security/claude-code-extension/remediate-macos.sh" download="">remediate-macos.sh</a> and run it as the affected user, not as root, from the folder you saved it to:</p>
<div class="prose-code-block"><pre class="shiki shiki-themes github-light github-dark" style="background-color:#fff;--shiki-dark-bg:#24292e;color:#24292e;--shiki-dark:#e1e4e8" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#6F42C1;--shiki-dark:#B392F0">bash</span><span style="color:#032F62;--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF"> remediate-macos.sh</span></span></code></pre></div>
<p>On Windows, download <a href="/static/security/claude-code-extension/remediate-windows.ps1" download="">remediate-windows.ps1</a> and run it from PowerShell opened with <strong>Run as Administrator</strong>, in the folder you saved it to:</p>
<div class="prose-code-block"><pre class="shiki shiki-themes github-light github-dark" style="background-color:#fff;--shiki-dark-bg:#24292e;color:#24292e;--shiki-dark:#e1e4e8" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8">powershell </span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">-</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8">ExecutionPolicy Bypass </span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">-</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8">File .\remediate</span><span style="color:#D73A49;--shiki-dark:#F97583">-</span><span style="color:#24292E;--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8">windows.ps1</span></span></code></pre></div>
<h2 id="indicators-of-compromise" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#indicators-of-compromise" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Indicators of compromise</h2>
<h3 id="package-version-21312" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#package-version-21312" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Package version 2.1.312</h3>
<ul>
<li>Modified VSIX SHA-256 (darwin-arm64): fcbb327e38e61c4fec795e0d0591f52cd1014b813d20a5912104953c3a17c364 (MD5 e0d64d53e802a0217ba6f0e656ed2f20)</li>
<li>Modified VSIX SHA-256 (win32-x64): 3de1722901165769893bef57c72594e9a54459faa23f3091b136b79966edd081 (MD5 bd3b71ddf3d0cc3af76249afd2c0eda1)</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="package-version-21313" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#package-version-21313" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Package version 2.1.313</h3>
<ul>
<li>Modified VSIX SHA-256 (darwin-arm64): 80402fdcad8799285fd93044976973ca000da7995fb93363f819bb8e4f84ee6c (MD5 34e491161e056c9b899a79b602ac73b9)</li>
<li>Modified VSIX SHA-256 (win32-x64): 6786ec90cbd45949695bd7805c9fbb26cfc91bc5fc897de0183d9bcb9cb21731 (MD5 7838a3be2ca0ff08c1bdb160ef516d39)</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="payload" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#payload" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Payload</h3>
<ul>
<li>Modified code: extension.js in package versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for both Darwin and Windows in the extension folder contains 134[.]209[.]82[.]225 and svc-telemetry</li>
<li>SHA-256: ecb58cb29078d9646ad1dcdbe51526f2d9cfea06be5fb2ab183e8ecc3ab6bf15</li>
<li>MD5: f49bcd657ef1e626e85ce858958c1769</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="network" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#network" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Network</h3>
<ul>
<li>Attacker endpoint: 134[.]209[.]82[.]225</li>
<li>Reverse SSH: tunnel@134[.]209[.]82[.]225, TCP 22</li>
<li>External beacon: hxxp://134[.]209[.]82[.]225:8099/beacon (HTTP POST)</li>
<li>Local beacon attempt: 127[.]0[.]0[.]1:8099/beacon (HTTP POST, loopback)</li>
<li>Public IP lookups to ifconfig[.]me / api[.]ipify[.]org — legitimate services; access alone is not an indicator</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="ssh" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#ssh" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>SSH</h3>
<ul>
<li>Unauthorized public key: <code>ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIDdvylCEJ/k2TpezcTfedrkHyFSK9IZ3vmP6vhY4Ss0P svc-telemetry</code></li>
<li>Unauthorized key fingerprint: <code>SHA256:0Z6R+DF64Do2nwQic8a7kkfDLNNk4IiK+2U2Rci4htk</code></li>
<li>Reverse-tunnel key fingerprint: <code>SHA256:KOAU57+ZG6u3MG4WwzPzPX2O5YEe9qdOC1Bl+6MVyDQ</code></li>
<li>Key comment: <code>svc-telemetry</code></li>
</ul>
<h3 id="files-and-persistence" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#files-and-persistence" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Files and persistence</h3>
<ul>
<li>Linux / macOS: unauthorized key in <code>~/.ssh/authorized_keys</code>; <code>~/.config/.smt</code>, <code>~/.config/.smtk</code></li>
<li>Linux: <code>/tmp/.stk_&lt;10 hex&gt;</code>; cron <code>@reboot /bin/sh &quot;&lt;HOME&gt;/.config/.smt&quot;</code></li>
<li>macOS: <code>$TMPDIR/.stk_&lt;10 hex&gt;</code>; <code>~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.apple.sysmond.plist</code> (label <code>com.apple.sysmond</code>)</li>
<li>Windows: <code>%USERPROFILE%\.ssh\authorized_keys</code>, <code>%USERPROFILE%\.config\smt.cmd</code>, <code>%USERPROFILE%\.config\smtk</code>, <code>%TEMP%\.stk_&lt;10 hex&gt;</code>; scheduled task <code>SysMon</code> (attempts to run as SYSTEM); fallback <code>%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\sysmon.cmd</code></li>
</ul>
<h3 id="process-command-line" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#process-command-line" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Process / command-line</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>ssh -N -R &#x27;*:0:localhost:22&#x27;</code>, <code>autossh -M 0</code></li>
<li>SSH options: <code>StrictHostKeyChecking=no</code>, <code>UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null</code>, <code>ServerAliveInterval=30</code>, <code>ServerAliveCountMax=3</code>, <code>ExitOnForwardFailure=yes</code>, <code>IdentitiesOnly=yes</code></li>
<li><code>schtasks /create /tn SysMon</code></li>
<li><code>systemsetup -setremotelogin on</code></li>
<li><code>Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Server~~~~0.0.1.0</code></li>
</ul>
<p>If you have further questions, reach out to <a href="mailto:security@cursor.com" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">security@cursor.com</a>.</p>
